ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Residual pigment in an aging cell

An autopsy specimen from an elderly patient shows fine yellow-brown perinuclear granules in cardiomyocytes. Iron staining is negative, and electron microscopy shows residual bodies containing incompletely degraded material. Which pigment best accounts for this finding?

  1. Lipofuscin
  2. Hemosiderin
  3. Melanin
  4. Bilirubin
  5. Carbon
Answer and explanation

Lipofuscin

Lipofuscin is a residual pigment associated with cumulative intracellular wear and oxidative damage.

Option explanations

Lipofuscin: Lipofuscin is a residual pigment associated with cumulative intracellular wear and oxidative damage.

Hemosiderin: Hemosiderin contains iron and would be detected by an appropriate iron stain.

Melanin: Melanin is not the usual perinuclear residual-body pigment of aging cardiomyocytes.

Bilirubin: Bilirubin deposition has a different distribution and clinical setting.

Carbon: Carbon typically accumulates after inhalation in lung-associated macrophages.
